title: Arithmetic Parser
description:
Implement `parse(tokens)` which takes an array of tokens (from a tokenizer) and returns an AST, and `evaluate(ast)` which evaluates the AST to a number.

The AST node format:
- Number: `{ type: 'number', value: number }`
- Binary: `{ type: 'binary', op: string, left: node, right: node }`

Operator precedence must be respected: `*` and `/` bind tighter than `+` and `-`.

**Example:**
```js
const tokens = [
  {type:'number',value:'1'},{type:'plus',value:'+'},
  {type:'number',value:'2'},{type:'star',value:'*'},
  {type:'number',value:'3'}
];
evaluate(parse(tokens)); // 7  (not 9)
```
ai_context: Most common mistake: not implementing recursive descent with separate precedence levels. Learners often parse left-to-right without a parseMulDiv layer, causing 1+2*3 to return 9 instead of 7.
